  component "LibrarianFactory\n(sets internalIdentifierCode)" as LFa
}

  component "User (abstract) / Student / Librarian\n(JPA, JOINED inheritance;\nunique email, studentNumber, code)" as Ent
  component "UserDTO\n(result returned to caller)" as DTO
}

package "Database" {
  component "PersistenceManager\n(findFirstByFields, save -> boolean)" as PM
  component "JpaUtil\n(EntityManagerFactory 'reservationsPU')" as JPA
}

U --> Swing

AC --> LF

LFa ..|> UF
LF --> UM

cat > view-2.puml <<'E'
@startuml
title View 2 - Registration collaboration: success and failure paths (UserManager.register)
actor Registrant
participant "Boundary\n(AuthenticationController / Swing Registration)" as B
participant LibraryFacade as LF
participant UserManager as UM
participant UserRegistry as UR
participant PersistenceManager as PM
participant "StudentFactory /\nLibrarianFactory" as F
database DB
participant RestExceptionHandler as REH

Registrant -> B : role, name, surname, email, password, identifier
B -> LF : register(...)
LF -> UM : register(...)
UM -> UM : validate(role, name, password)\nrole in {Student, Librarian}, name set,\npassword 8..32
alt invalid role / name / password
  UM --> B : IllegalArgumentException
else role = Student
  UM -> UM : validateStudent: name/surname letters<=20,\nemail @*.unina.it (<255), id = [A-Z]\\d{8}
else role = Librarian
  UM -> UM : validateLibrarian: name/surname, email,\nid alphanumeric non-empty
end
alt format validation fails
  UM --> B : IllegalArgumentException(message)
end
UM -> UR : institutionalEmailExists(email)
UR -> PM : findFirstByFields(User, institutionalEmail)
PM -> DB : SELECT
DB --> PM
PM --> UR
UR --> UM : exists?
alt email already registered
  UM --> B : IllegalArgumentException\n"Email is already associated with an account."
end
UM -> UR : findStudentByStudentNumber(id) /\nfindLibrarianByCode(id)
UR -> PM : findFirstByFields(Student|Librarian, ...)
PM -> DB : SELECT
UR --> UM : existing?
alt identifier already used
  UM --> B : IllegalArgumentException\n"Identifier is already in use."
end
UM -> F : createUser(name, surname, email, password, identifier)
F --> UM : Student | Librarian (not yet persisted)
UM -> UR : registerUser(newUser)
UR -> PM : save(newUser)
PM -> DB : persist in transaction
alt persistence fails (e.g. unique constraint)
  PM --> UR : false (rollback)
  UR --> UM : false
  UM --> B : RuntimeException "Server error: ... could not be saved"
else saved
  PM --> UR : true
  UR --> UM : true
  UM --> B : UserDTO (id, role, identifier)
end
note over B, REH
 Web: IllegalArgumentException -> RestExceptionHandler -> HTTP 400 {"error": msg}.
 A plain RuntimeException (save failure) is NOT mapped by the handler.
 Swing: catches RuntimeException and shows message dialog.
end note
@enduml
E
cat > README.md <<'E'
# User registration - architecture views (IS-reg-L3)

Source: `JavaProject/src/main/java/it/unina/reservations` (layers: boundary / controller / entity / database).

- **view-1.puml - Component view.** Shows who receives the registration request (web form -> `AuthenticationController`, or Swing `Registration`), the `LibraryFacade` entry point, `UserManager` (validation of personal data and role, role-specific identifier rules, uniqueness checks), the `UserFactory` implementations (`StudentFactory`/`LibrarianFactory`, which set `studentNumber` / `internalIdentifierCode`), `UserRegistry` + `PersistenceManager` + `JpaUtil` (persistence in MySQL) and `RestExceptionHandler` (error mapping). Why: gives the tester the components, responsibilities, dependencies and the integration seams (boundary->facade->manager, manager->registry->persistence->DB, manager->factories).
- **view-2.puml - Sequence view of the collaboration.** Shows the ordered checks in `UserManager.register` and what happens for invalid data (role/name/password/format), duplicate email, duplicate student ID / librarian code, and a failed save, with the exception returned to each boundary. Why: identifies which interactions each negative/positive integration test must exercise (e.g. email lookup via `UserRegistry`->`PersistenceManager`; unique-constraint failure path returning `false`).

Notes for testing: duplicate checks run before persistence, so the DB unique constraints (email, studentNumber, code) are only a second line of defence; a failed save raises a `RuntimeException` that `RestExceptionHandler` does not map (only IllegalArgument/IllegalState -> 400). Existing `RegistrationTest` calls the controller layer against a real DB (MySQL per persistence.xml).
E

content.text:
I wrote two PlantUML views and a README, but I haven't rendered the diagrams to check that they compile.

The files are in `task2view-out/IS-reg-L3/` inside the repository folder:

- **`view-1.puml` (component view):**
  - **Request entry:** the web form (`registration.html` posting to `/auth/register` through `AuthenticationController`) or the Swing `Registration` form. Both call `LibraryFacade`.
  - **Validation and uniqueness:** `UserManager` checks the role, name, surname, email, password and identifier rules, then checks for an existing email and identifier.
  - **Role-specific data:** `StudentFactory` sets the student number and `LibrarianFactory` sets the librarian code.
  - **Persistence:** `UserRegistry`, `PersistenceManager` and `JpaUtil` save the user to MySQL.
  - **Error mapping:** `RestExceptionHandler` maps invalid input to HTTP 400.
- **`view-2.puml` (sequence view):** the order of the checks in `UserManager.register`, and what each boundary receives in each failure case:
  - invalid role, name or password
  - a format error in the student ID, librarian code or email
  - duplicate email
  - duplicate identifier
  - a failed save
  - success

Two behaviours matter for your tests:

- **Duplicates caught early:** duplicate email and identifier are caught by lookups before the save. The database unique constraints are only a second line of defence.
- **Unmapped save failure:** a failed save throws a plain `RuntimeException`, which `RestExceptionHandler` does not map. Only `IllegalArgumentException` and `IllegalStateException` become a 400 response.

The README explains what each view shows and why.
